script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 26. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Einstein said if he had one hour to save the world, he'd spend 55 minutes defining the problem and 5 minutes solving it.  The quality of your questions determines the quality of your answers—and ultimately, the quality of your life.

Einstein, Darwin, and Newton all emphasized question-framing over answer-finding. A poorly framed question leads to useless answers. A well-framed question often reveals its own answer. The hard work is in the asking. Yes-or-no questions shut down thinking.  Open questions—'how might we...
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Instead of seeking answers, become a collector of better questions.  'Why?
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Question Upgrade - Better Inquiries.

Here's your activity: Take a problem you're facing and write down the question you've been asking about it. Then reframe it three different ways—make it broader, make it more specific, make it about possibility. Notice which reframe feels most useful. This helps you improve the quality of questions you ask.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about the power of good questions can be applied to question upgrade - better inquiries. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
